en.name: Dominic Savio
en.summary: Young student of John Bosco whose intense but cheerful piety made him, at his death at fourteen, one of the Church's youngest confessor saints.
en.body: Dominic Savio was a poor blacksmith's son who walked several miles each day to attend school before being accepted, at John Bosco's personal invitation, into the boarding oratory Bosco ran for at-risk youth in Turin, where he quickly stood out for a combination of ordinary boyish energy, he organized other boys into a mutual-support club against bullying and bad influences, and unusually intense personal devotion, reportedly resolving as a small child that he would rather die than commit a serious sin. Bosco, who came to regard him as a model of the balanced, joyful holiness he hoped to form in all his students, later wrote a widely read biography of him after his early death. Dominic's health was always fragile, and he died at home in 1857 at only fourteen, having contracted a lung ailment. He was canonized in 1954, becoming one of the youngest saints in Church history to be canonized as a confessor, meaning through the ordinary holiness of daily life rather than martyrdom.
